questions.prompt: A stored-program computer keeps the instructions of a program where?
options: In a plugboard that is rewired for every new program
In memory, so the same hardware can run different programs
Only inside the ALU, which rewrites them as it executes
In the power supply, which sequences the clock
questions.explanation: The program counter fetches instructions from memory. Load a different bit pattern and the same processor runs a different program.
traps: The ALU operates on bits; it is not the program store.

questions.prompt: Which order matches one ordinary instruction cycle?
questions.explanation: The CPU reads the instruction word, works out what it means, then carries it out. The next fetch uses the updated program counter.
traps: Decode cannot run before the instruction has been read.

questions.prompt: Which of these are parts of a typical system bus?
questions.explanation: Address lines name a location, data lines carry the word, and control lines say whether this is a read, a write, or a similar action.
traps: A compiler is software, not a set of wires.

questions.prompt: The phrase “von Neumann bottleneck” points at which limit?
options: Instructions and data share one path to memory
Disks spin slower than the clock, and that is the whole story
A process is allowed only one thread
questions.explanation: One memory interface serves both instruction fetches and data loads, so the processor often waits on that shared path.

questions.prompt: A service answers each request in 4 ms and finishes 200 requests a second. The 4 ms figure is
questions.explanation: Latency is the wait for one operation. Throughput counts how many finish per unit of time. A busy service can have both a queue and a high completion rate.
traps: A large throughput number does not tell you the wait for a single request.

questions.prompt: Which of these are hardware in a typical computer?
questions.explanation: The kernel is software that is loaded into memory. The processor, memory, and device controllers are hardware.
traps: The operating system is essential, and it is still software.

questions.prompt: During a normal fetch, the program counter holds
options: The opcode of the instruction that just finished
The address of the next instruction to read
The result of the last ALU operation
questions.explanation: The program counter is an address. The instruction bits themselves are copied into the instruction register.
traps: The program counter does not store the instruction word.

questions.prompt: Which statement about a machine word is the reliable one?
options: A word is always one byte
A word is the width the machine commonly treats as a unit, and that width depends on the machine
A word is the size of a disk sector
questions.explanation: A byte is 8 bits by modern convention. Word size is an architectural choice: both 32-bit and 64-bit machines are ordinary.
traps: “A word is 16 bits” is a habit from one generation of machines, not a rule.

questions.prompt: Why is it useful that instructions live in the same memory as data?
questions.answer: The processor can treat a program as data: load it, switch it, or generate it, without rewiring the hardware.
questions.explanation: That is the stored-program idea. The machine does not need a new circuit for each program; it needs a new bit pattern in memory.
